text.text: Came to MDK Noodle on the Fourth of July at 4 p.m. expecting to fight for a table and instead had the run of the place — turns out "everyone's at a barbecue" is my favorite reservation strategy. I ordered the spicy knife-cut noodles in chicken broth (the spicy kalguksu), which billed itself as spicy and then negotiated me down to "spicy enough" — respectable heat that talks a big game but lets you keep your dignity and your taste buds. The hand-cut noodles landed somewhere between okay and genuinely good, which is a weirdly specific and honest place for a noodle to be, and I mean that as a compliment. The lighting is bright enough to read the fine print on your life choices, the broth had a real kick without staging a coup, and the whole thing earns a solid four stars across the board. Would slurp again — preferably next time a national holiday empties the room for me.

text.text:
Better than the Seoul outposts imo.

MDK noodles in LA's Koreatown is a staple for me when in the area. In fact, I've drove quite far out of the way to go here. I've probably been here 8 times or so.

I've been to the same restaurants in Korea's Myeongdong area about the same number of times. Both serve kalguksu soups and mandu. The LA location has more items on its menu, including alcohol.

MDK noodle may not be the absolute best Kalguksu around, but it's consistent, delicious and satisfying comfort food. Their mandu is also excellent.

Interestingly, in Korea, I prefer the non-spicy version while in LA I prefer the spicy version.

people say this is one of the best Korean spots. So let’s see if they’re pretty good eh or ew. The servers were really attentive and I got their chive pancake, meats and kimchi dumplings, jengban neang myun, and galbi Jim to try. Course we gotta start with their crunchy but not too fermented cabbage and radish kimchi and soft steamed cabbage with soybean paste. The chive pancake was savory and green oniony and was lightly crisp and chewy. Paired well with the oniony soy saucy vinegary dipping sauce. The dumplings had chewy doughy skins with umami meaty fillings. The kimchi one was just a bit spicy. The jengban neang myun was refreshing and had qq thin noodles, thinly sliced beef and radish slices, squiggy not fishy raw fish, and crisp Korean pear sticks. And finally for my fave Korean dish galbi Jim. It came with some pretty purple rice and I added super gooey stretchy mozzarella cheese to it and it wasn’t spicy but was very flavorful and had soft tender onions, startchy potatoes, sweet pumpkin, bouncy rice cakes, and fall of the bone beef ribs. MNM. Overall this place is pretty good.

Hot summer day and a few of us wanted cold noodles, so we thought we would try Lee Ga and see if the hype was real. While the broth was tasty, it wasn’t cold :( Kind of defeats the purpose, especially when you’re waiting in the heat for a table and the room itself was pretty warm. Banchan was pretty limited as well, with just two Kim chi types and cucumbers with samjang. The highlight might have been the ribs, which are not LA style but full bone. The bulgogi was pretty tasty as well, but serving was really small and the daengjang soup not all that great. Loved the purple rice though! I do like that they offer free tea, but is offset with the charging of to go boxes :). I realize it’s only $0.50, but it did keep me from ordering an extra dish which would have guaranteed the need for containers. Thankfully we only needed three :).

Parking is valet only and the place was packed even though we chose an off peak time of 2:00pm. $3 isn’t bad, but even valet had a hard time keeping up so keep parking in mind when visiting.

This place is truly a local gem. If you’re looking for real, authentic Korean food, this restaurant delivers in every way. You can taste the difference the moment your meal arrives—everything is made with the freshest, highest-quality ingredients, and it really shows.
The standout for me is the gukbap. There’s a warmth and affection in every bowl that feels like something straight from a Korean home kitchen. It’s the kind of comfort food that hugs you from the inside out—rich broth, perfectly balanced flavors, and ingredients that taste like they were prepped just hours before.
And don’t even get me started on the lunch specials—they are unbelievably worth it. Generous portions, great variety, and prices that make you feel like you’re getting way more than you paid for. It’s become my go-to midday spot because the quality and value are unbeatable.

Everything we ate and drank was fantastic as was the service!

They had a talented vinyl DJ playing for most of the time we were there, and I was shocked and impressed to learn he was the owner 😅 I was also surprised by our final bill, which was shockingly affordable, especially for DTLA. We’ll 1000% be back!

text.text:
I’ve been to Escala in Koreatown a few times before, but this visit meant so much more because I brought my aunt, kids, and family to celebrate my aunt’s birthday. We’re all Colombian, and while we absolutely love our food, I really wanted them to experience Korean cuisine — and Escala did not disappoint.

The food was incredible, full of flavor, and honestly felt so homey and comforting. Everyone at the table loved what they ordered. Even my toddler and her cousins had the best time — the music and atmosphere made it such a fun space where they could enjoy themselves without feeling stuck at the table.

My aunt’s dish did come out later than the rest of ours, but we truly didn’t mind because the place was busy and everything we had tasted so amazing. What really stood out, though, was the level of care and service we received.

On my way to the bathroom, I recognized the owner and chef from social media and stopped to share how much I loved the food and the vibe. They were so warm and even asked if we were Colombian, which made the experience feel instantly more personal.

The highlight of the night was the chef — she went out of her way to come to our table, introduce herself, and genuinely connect with us. When she found out about my aunt’s delayed plate, she immediately took care of it and didn’t charge us, which we didn’t expect at all. It was such a kind gesture and showed how much pride and love she puts into what she does — truly taking care of people like family.

As we were leaving, she even came to find us to say goodbye. That level of attention and heart is something you don’t see everywhere.

Escala isn’t just amazing food — it’s an experience filled with warmth, culture, and genuine hospitality. We felt like family, and I will absolutely keep coming back.

We enjoyed our meal so much that we almost ran late for our concert afterward — that’s how good it was!

Highly recommend Soban if you’re looking for an experience that’s not only delicious, but heartfelt and memorable. This is a place you’ll want to return to again and again.

I've always enjoyed Soowon (or Suwon, a suburb of Seoul) style galbi over regular Korean bbq marinated meat. It's sweeter and much more flavorful. It's also less well known but there are more of Suwon style galbi places even in the Bay Area. But since I'm here in LA, of course I'll look up a Suwon galbi place here in ktown. The parking is annoying as you have to valet it but it's probably a necessity due to how small the parking lot is.

I highly recommend the marinated galbi as almost everything else you can have at any other Korean bbq restaurant.

I had high hopes and a lot of excitement for Lapaba and am sad to report that I left quite disappointed! As someone who loves trying new and interesting menus, Italian Korean fusion sounded delicious.

The good:
I saw previous reviews that complained about portion sizes, but we were happy with the portion sizes we got. Good sharing size for two.
The price was very reasonable for two people who each got a NA drink, shared two starters and three pastas, including the lobster dish.
There’s decent street parking available along with valet out front.
The interior is simple, trendy, and nice. It’s mainly one looong pasta bar, best for a two person dinner or a date night.
I tried the Yakult mocktail and really liked it.

The meh:
Sadly, the food. A friend and I shared the fried chicken and burrata starters and the cheesy corn agnolotti, radiatore and galbi jjim (short rib), and the lobster and tonnarelli. The fried chicken lollipops were our favorite bite for dinner, the sweet chili sauce flavor was great. The burrata is served on top of a slice of sweet potato with chili crisp and soy. It sounded like a fun dish, but we both only tasted sweet potato.

Unfortunately none of the pastas were great. The radiatore galbi jjim dish was my favorite pasta of the trio, but it was at best like a nice meat sauce pasta. I did not like either the agnolotti or the lobster tonnarelli. As someone who loves a corn agnolotti, the main flavor of the agnolotti was a burnt flavor, strangely. It was lacking in both “cheesy” and corn flavor. The lobster had a slightly fishy flavor and the tonnarelli pasta was forgettable. I would skip both.

We decided to skip dessert and grab soft serve next door. My hope is that Lapaba can improve their menu to really nail Italian and Korean fusion, but for now it’s not a spot I’d recommend.

We were super excited to dine at this new Korean Italian fusion restaurant. The restaurant is basically one large pasta bar and was well decorated. We ordered two of their pasta dishes and a few of their starters to share.

While the main focus on the menu were the pastas, it felt like they only added a Korean ingredient to make it different rather than try to make the dishes feel authentically “fusion”. They were tasty but the flavors definitely lean traditional Italian.

The starters were definitely where the fusion comes in. Echoing the same point as before but the flavor of the kimchi in the suppli was also very subtle. The most “fused” dish was the K meatballs that tasted like bulgogi and were paired with a traditional red sauce. The bread it came with was tasty but didn’t have the most shiny/golden crust.

We got a few of their drinks (yuja sour, arancia yakult, matcha yuja-ade) and they were good but very very sweet.

We ended with the BTS (black truffle soft serve) which was a lovely balance of sweet and savory.

TLDR: flavors were good but the dishes didnt feel like a true fusion experience. We felt like the menu lacked intention.

The place looks nice and clean, and the prices are acceptable—we spent $117 for two people, which included:
•	🥩 Marinated Short Ribs – $25

Honestly, if the staff are having a hard day, they should just stay home. There’s no need to show up and give customers that kind of attitude.

We came in expecting a decent Korean BBQ experience. Instead, we got so-so meat and bad service. Won’t be returning.

I had one of the best kbbq experiences here. We went at 1:30pm on a Tuesday and there was no wait. For 3 people, we ordered a small gopchang set and a small beef set plus a kimchi pancake. It was a good amount of food for us.

The food quality is good and what makes the experience unforgettable is the incredible service. The guy cooking for us prepared the food with so much care and precision. He would rotate the meat to make sure they’re cooked evenly. Even though he was helping several tables, I never got the sense that he was rushed or annoyed. Always super attentive and professional.

Back to the food- the set meals come with a soup and steam egg. I like the doenjang-jjigae the most. All the beef cuts we got were great but my favorite is the skirt steak for sure - very flavorful, not too fatty. The gopchang set came with small intestines, less fatty and more on the grainy side, just the way I like it. If you prefer the fattier one, go for the large intestines. The rice cakes and veggies cooked in the intestine fat were also super yummy. Kimchi fried rice at the end was A++.

I’d happily come back again and again.

The Sizzle of Sophistication: An In-Depth Masterclass in Meat at Ahgassi Gopchang

In a culinary landscape often dominated by the overwhelming "quantity over quality" ethos of buffet-style dining, **Ahgassi Gopchang** emerges as a distinguished oasis for the discerning meat lover. This establishment offers far more than just a meal; it curates an extraordinary dining experience, expertly blending fire, fat, and an explosion of flavors that delight the senses.

**The Strategic Entry**
Entering Ahgassi Gopchang is an event that requires patience, often featuring **two-hour wait times**. We avoided this by making a reservation. Upon entering, we were greeted by a vibrant atmosphere and sophisticated design, where booking ahead is essential for a smooth culinary experience.

**Precision at the Grill**
Ahgassi Gopchang stands out by having skilled servers handle the grill, eliminating the "amateur grill-master" experience. Each cut of meat is expertly grilled to perfection, allowing the savory juices to shine through. This attention to detail creates a memorable dining experience, letting diners focus on their companions and the artistry of the meal.

The Menu: A Study in Marbling and Marinade
Ahgassi Gopchang consciously chooses to move away from the all-you-can-eat model, favoring instead a well-thought-out **a la carte menu** along with carefully curated combo packages. This approach allows the kitchen to dedicate itself to the integrity and quality of each protein that hits the grill. Our tasting journey comprised a thoughtfully selected progression of meats, each offering a unique symphony of textures and flavors:

* **The Marinated Brisket & Bulgogi:** The brisket was cut with surgical thinness, enabling it to sear almost instantly and capture the essence of the grill. The bulgogi served as a delightful counterpart, showcasing a classic blend of sweet and savory flavors that epitomize the essence of elite Korean barbecue.

* **The Marinated Hanger Filet:** This cut stood out for its robust and hearty flavor, often referred to as the "butcher's cut." The marinade was expertly balanced, enhancing the meat's natural flavors without overpowering them, making it a must-try for anyone serious about quality beef.

* **The Short Rib:** Undoubtedly the crown jewel of our meal, the short rib boasted perfect marbling and was handled with exceptional care on the grill. Each bite practically dissolved in your mouth, a testament to both the quality of the meat and the skill of the grill masters.

To complement our meat-centric feast, the supporting dishes were equally impressive. The **steamed egg** arrived at our table like a golden cloud—its texture was light and airy, with a delicate savory flavor that served as a delightful counterpoint to the richness of the meats. Meanwhile, the **tofu soup** contributed a spicy, soul-warming complexity, rounding out our meal and ensuring that each bite was balanced and satisfying.

The Verdict: A Perfect 10/10

From the vibrant, high-energy ambiance to the meticulous precision of the service, Ahgassi Gopchang provided an **unforgettable 10/10 experience**. This is a rare destination where the buzz of the crowd is not just a trend but is genuinely validated by the exceptional quality of food served. For those who appreciate the nuances of a perfect sear and the luxury of professional table-side service, this is undoubtedly the premier destination for Korean barbecue.

*Do yourself a favor: make that reservation, skip the line, and allow the professionals at Ahgassi Gopchang to showcase how Korean barbecue is meant to be savored.*

This place has been on my list for at least a year, but I didn’t get around to visiting until I got the red dining book for Christmas. The place exceeded all expectations. It’s very tiny, with a big bar and only a few tables. They accept reservations and I highly recommend making one, otherwise you might find yourself lining out of the door. Everybody there is just vibing. Because the place is so small, all the staff members know exactly how many people they have, their order and the status of each dish. The service was quick, super friendly, and the owner came up to chat with us for a while and signed my book himself, it felt so very special. The food and drinks are incredible! We had to get tteokbokki with sea urchin row sauce, and their kimchi a la vodka. Both dishes were so good that I desperately wished for a piece of bread or a bit of rice to soak up every last drop of the sauces. I ended up asking for a spoon… portions are not huge, one entry is perfect for one person. We also got a couple of their drinks, both tasted very good but not enough spirit-forward to my taste, next time I’ll stick to straight soju or makgeolli, they have a great selection. Parking is everything you should expect from Koreatown, meter or street parking which takes time to find.
Can’t wait to be back!!

If you plan to dine at Chi Chi LA, remember this: Reservation is a must! This place gets incredibly busy on weekends, and it's no wonder why. Chi Chi LA is a restaurant like no other, offering an extraordinary blend of dining and entertainment.

The atmosphere on a weekend night is positively vibrant and bustling. The reason? Well, it's all thanks to the special feature at every table – the personal ordering devices. These nifty gadgets aren't just for placing your food orders; they're a gateway to a world of fun and games.

Each table has its own ordering device, which not only allows you to select your dishes but also provides a variety of interactive games. You can enjoy mini-games by yourself or challenge other tables. There are even spontaneous group challenges initiated by the restaurant. Plus, there's a chat room where you can strike up conversations with diners at other tables.

Now, onto the food. Chi Chi LA offers a tasty menu, though portions are on the smaller side. The flavors are delightful, and I highly recommend trying their flavored Soju cocktails. They come with eye-catching glowing lights and adorable duck decorations that add a cute touch to your dining experience.

The only drawback is that engaging in conversation can be a bit challenging due to the continuous sounds of excitement from people playing games all around you. But if you're here for a fun and interactive dining adventure, this might not bother you too much.
